title: Year 11 Investigating Science Module 4 – Theories and Laws
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 11 Investigating Science Module 4. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What type of scientific explanation gives a broad account of how or why phenomena occur?
What type of scientific statement describes a consistent relationship in nature?
What kind of data must support scientific theories and laws?
Which usually explains phenomena: a theory or a law?
Which is often expressed as a mathematical relationship: a theory or a law?
What theory explains disease as being caused by microorganisms?
What theory explains combustion using oxygen rather than phlogiston?
What old solar-system theory placed Earth at the centre?
What rejected theory proposed that acquired characteristics could be inherited?
questions.answer: The inheritance of acquired characteristics. Accept: Lamarckism.

questions.prompt: What cosmological theory proposed that the Universe stays broadly the same as it expands?
What law states that mass is conserved in a closed system during ordinary chemical reactions?
questions.answer: The law of conservation of mass.

questions.prompt: What law relates force, mass and acceleration?
What law states that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of particles?
What geological law says younger sedimentary layers usually lie above older layers?
What electrical law relates voltage, current and resistance?
What theory explains the movement of Earth’s lithospheric plates?
questions.answer: Plate tectonic theory. Accept: plate tectonics.

questions.prompt: What theory explains changes in populations over generations?
What theory explains the origin and expansion of the Universe from an early hot, dense state?
What theory describes matter as being made of atoms?
What can happen to a scientific theory when strong new evidence contradicts part of it?
questions.answer: It can be revised or rejected. Accept: modified, refined or disproved in part.

questions.prompt: What law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or transformed?
questions.answer: The law of conservation of energy.

questions.prompt: Which science discipline studies conservation of energy in motion, forces and physical systems?
Which science discipline applies conservation of energy to chemical reactions?
Which science discipline applies energy conservation to processes such as metabolism?
What type of nuclear process helped change how scientists interpret conservation of mass and energy?
questions.answer: Nuclear reactions and decay. Accept: nuclear reactions or radioactive decay.

finalRound.prompt: What key feature of scientific data allows other scientists to obtain consistent results and build confidence in theories and laws?
finalRound.answer: Reproducibility. Accept: reproducible data or reproducible results.
